<xpln lang="en"><etym lang="tbd">[<term lang="du">oester</term>, Dutch; <term lang="fr">huitre</term>, Fr.:]</etym> A bivalve testa­
ceous fish.
<term lang="quo">I will not lend thee a penny—
—Why then the world's mine oyster which
I with sword will open. Shakesp. Merr. W. of Wind.</term>
<term lang="quo">Rich honesty dwells like your miser, sir, in a poor house;
as your pearl in your foul oyster. Shakesp.</term>
<term lang="quo">Another mass held a kind of oyster shell, and other bivalves.
Woodward on Fossils.</term>
<term lang="quo">There may be as many ranks of beings in the invisible
world superior to us, as we are superior to all the ranks of
being in this visible world; though we descend below the
oyster to the least animated atoms discovered by microscopes.
Watts's Improv. of the Mind.</term>
<term lang="quo">Where oyster tubs in rows
Are rang'd beside the posts, there stay thy haste. Gay.</term></xpln>
